solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bottom falling out of side dish

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom is the final letter, and falling out means it drops away

blocks.note: a flank is the side of an army or a body

explanation.surface: A side dish whose base has collapsed, a kitchen disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side dish' reads as one phrase, but 'side' is the wordplay and 'dish' alone is the definition; FLANK loses its last letter K.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open pastry or sponge case with a filling, served as a sweet or savoury course.

clue.text: Idiot interrupting very timid creature, right menace

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: the hare is proverbially timid and quick to bolt
an ass is a fool
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A fool bothering a nervous animal, a real menace to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Menace' here is a noun for a person who menaces, not the verb; the hare's timidity is proverbial, which is why 'very timid creature' points to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A harasser is someone who persistently pesters or intimidates others, which makes them a threat or nuisance.

clue.text: Harm that comes from the woman embracing tiger?

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug and enclose, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: the pronoun for a woman
a tiger is one example of a big cat, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A lady hugging a tiger is asking to get hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a tiger is only one kind of CAT, a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: To scathe is an old verb meaning to injure or damage, surviving mainly in 'unscathed'.

clue.text: Member of secret society eating fish, ending with the cheese

indicators.note: something that eats takes food inside itself, so one piece goes within another
an ending is the final part of a word, so just its closing letter is kept
with means alongside, so the next piece is simply attached

blocks.note: a Freemason, member of a famously secretive fraternity
the carp is a freshwater fish
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Freemason eats fish and finishes the meal with cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ending with the cheese' reads as the end of a meal, but 'ending' takes only the last letter of 'the', leaving 'cheese' alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascarpone is a soft, creamy Italian dairy product used in tiramisu, one kind of cheese.

clue.text: Cabbage and rolled-up meat served to daughter

indicators.note: food served to someone is placed next to them, so one piece follows the other

blocks.note: collar is a cut of bacon or beef usually rolled and tied
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A family meal: greens and a rolled joint dished up to the daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Collar is a butcher's term for a rolled joint, especially collar of bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: Collard is a loose-leafed variety of kale or cabbage, eaten as collard greens in the American South.

clue.text: Not an original individual about to get detached from others

indicators.note: one thing getting another simply adds it on, so the pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
alone, set apart from everyone else

explanation.surface: Someone unoriginal is about to be cut off from the group.
explanation.walkthrough: C for circa, meaning about, is standard in dates.
explanation.definitionFit: A clone is an exact genetic copy of another organism, so it is a duplicate rather than the first.

clue.text: One with an eye for embroidery?

definitions.text: One with an eye for embroidery?

blocks.clueFragment: One with an eye for embroidery?
blocks.note: surface reading: a person with good taste in needlework
setter's reading: a sewing tool with a hole for thread, used to mend fabric

explanation.surface: Praising a craftsperson who has real taste in decorative stitching.
explanation.walkthrough: An eye for something usually means an aptitude; here it is the literal hole in a sewing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large sewing implement with a long eye, used for mending holes in socks and knitwear with wool.

clue.text: Laugh at / rubbish

blocks.note: first meaning: to tease or banter with someone
second meaning: husks and worthless matter separated from grain

explanation.walkthrough: The slash marks the join between two separate meanings of one word, a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to mock good-humouredly; as a noun it is the discarded husks of threshed corn, hence worthless stuff.

clue.text: In the hills that hurts chaps

indicators.note: one thing being in another places it within, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: fells are hills or moorland in northern England
the cry of someone in pain

explanation.surface: Hiking men complaining that the hills are painful.
explanation.walkthrough: FELLS, the Lake District word for hills, holds the exclamation OW.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellows and chaps are both informal British words for men in general.

clue.text: Lizard? Don’t hang around, girl!

blocks.note: an order to leave at once
a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone spots a lizard and urges a girl to get moving.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often use 'girl' for any female name that fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Goanna is the Australian name for a monitor, a large carnivorous reptile of the lizard family.

clue.text: Networks broadcasting recital, including Schubert’s 4th

indicators.note: an ordinal picks out a single letter by its position in the name
broadcasting scatters things widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
S-C-H-U: the fourth letter

explanation.surface: TV and radio networks airing a concert that features a Schubert symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Networks broadcasting' sounds like TV stations; 'Schubert's 4th' is not his symphony but his name's fourth letter, added to the letters of 'recital'.
explanation.definitionFit: Reticula is the plural of reticulum, a Latin word for a fine net-like structure or mesh.

clue.text: Liberal agent brought back message

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the way it came, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative, an agent
a missive is a letter or message

explanation.surface: A political party's envoy returning with a communication.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on 'Liberal' suggests the political party, but it is simply the adjective meaning tolerant.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe an attitude that allows freedom and tolerates behaviour others might forbid.

clue.text: A false man, servant ultimately sacked?

definitions.text: A false man, servant ultimately sacked?

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept
a sacked town is plundered and thrown into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A dishonest servant who ended up being dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a false man, a servant who might well get the sack, describes the wrongdoer.
explanation.definitionFit: A malfeasant is a person guilty of wrongdoing, especially an official who abuses a position of trust.

clue.text: Sleeping place that lacks sun — it’s underground

indicators.note: to lack something is to be without it, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: a roost is where birds sleep
S is the abbreviation for sun

explanation.surface: A dark underground bedroom with no sunlight.
explanation.walkthrough: S for sun is removed from ROOST; the definition is a descriptive phrase for the thing, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant's roots grow beneath the soil, anchoring it and drawing up water, so this is what lies below ground.

clue.text: If ruthless ego gets out of hand, one gets smug

indicators.note: something out of hand is out of control, so these letters run riot into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Letting a ruthless ego run wild makes a person complacent.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like moral advice, but the first three words supply exactly the thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone complacently convinced of their own virtue and superiority over others.

clue.text: Performances to include commercial tracks

indicators.note: to include something is to take it in, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: shows are performances
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: Shows that feature commercials between their musical tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tracks' looks like a plural noun for songs, but it is a verb: follows closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow someone is to follow them secretly, the way a detective tails or pursues a suspect.

clue.text: International on the box that may set a precedent

indicators.note: in a down entry one thing on another sits above it, so the pieces are stacked in order

blocks.note: a Test is an international cricket or rugby match
a case is a box or container

explanation.surface: An international match on television could set a trend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the box' suggests on TV, but the box is just a case; a Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A test case is a legal action whose outcome establishes a principle that later courts will follow.

clue.text: This underlying structure sounds deep

indicators.note: sounds means is heard like, so the word is identified by its pronunciation

blocks.note: a deep voice or note is bass, pronounced like the answer

explanation.surface: A foundation that sounds profound.
explanation.walkthrough: BASS, the low singing voice, is said the same way as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A base is the foundation or bottom support on which a structure rests.

clue.text: It’s right for us to say what we want

definitions.text: It’s right for us to say what we want

blocks.clueFragment: It’s right for us to say what we want
blocks.note: surface reading: an opinion that people should voice their wishes
setter's reading: the right in question is a civil liberty of expression

explanation.surface: Someone insisting it is proper for us to speak our minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' reads as 'correct' but is a noun: the entitlement itself.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the civil liberty to express opinions without censorship or restraint by the state.

clue.text: Workman / better equipped

blocks.note: first meaning: a mechanic who assembles or installs machinery
second meaning: more suitable, comparative of an adjective

explanation.walkthrough: The slash separates a noun meaning a tradesman from a comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A fitter installs and repairs equipment; as a comparative adjective it means more suitable or more capable.

clue.text: Man in Australian location sacrificing little son

indicators.note: sacrificing something means giving it up, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: A city in Queensland, Australia
S is the short form of son

explanation.surface: A man in an Australian town giving up his young boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person; in northern English hill country a man is a pile of stones marking a summit.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cumbrian and Scottish usage, 'man' names a heap of stones built on a hilltop as a landmark.

clue.text: Bodily restricted, being fixed by side of table, bound by string

indicators.note: a side is an edge, so one letter at the edge of the word is taken
by means next to, so the pieces are placed alongside
something bound is tied up all round, so a piece is wrapped inside another

blocks.note: cord is string
set means fixed firmly
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone strapped to the edge of a table with string, unable to move.
explanation.walkthrough: SET plus the end letter of 'table' is wrapped in CORD.
explanation.definitionFit: A corseted body is laced into a tight undergarment that constricts the waist and torso.

clue.text: Port with a hundred and one smuggled aboard unfortunately

indicators.note: contraband smuggled aboard is hidden inside the vessel, so a piece goes within another

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
alas expresses regret
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cross-Channel port where, sadly, a hundred and one items were smuggled onto a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The smuggling scene suits a ferry port; I goes inside ALAS, with C in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Calais is the French ferry port on the English Channel, closest to Dover.

clue.text: Tree in white caustic earth

blocks.note: first meaning: the linden, a broad-leaved tree
second meaning: quicklime, calcium oxide

explanation.surface: A tree growing in pale, burning soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is only a link between the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The linden is also called by this name, and so is calcium oxide, a white alkaline substance burnt from limestone.

clue.text: Discernment to think about conflicting directions

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: 'I see' can mean 'I think' or understand
north and south, opposed compass points

explanation.surface: Good judgment means weighing up contradictory instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: North and south point opposite ways, which is what makes them conflicting.
explanation.definitionFit: Good sense and discernment both mean sound practical judgement and perception.

clue.text: Early developer, me — Santa found out!

indicators.note: being found out upsets a plan, so these letters are thrown into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A precocious child boasts of discovering the truth about Father Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early developer' sounds like a precocious child, but it is George Eastman, the Kodak founder who pioneered photographic film.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eastman founded Kodak and popularised roll film, so he was a pioneer in developing photographs.
